meta_title: GoodChess — chess with an AI coach
meta_description: Play the Stockfish engine and 13 bots, solve 50,000 Lichess puzzles, play rated games online. An AI coach explains every move in plain words.
hero_sub: Play the engine, solve puzzles and review your games with an AI coach. It talks in words, not evaluation numbers.
hero_aside: On the board: Morphy's “Opera Game”, Paris, 1858. The coach is reviewing it right now.
scene_label: Demo: the “Opera Game”, Paul Morphy vs the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard, Paris, 1858
intro: Let's watch Morphy's “Opera Game”. I'll tell you where a move is strong and where it's a mistake.
note_1: The centre, and open lines for the bishop and queen at once. A good start.
note_6: The pin looks active, but the bishop will soon trade itself for the knight — and White gains time to develop.
note_12: The knight blocks the queen, and f7 stays weak. Watch the bishop on c4.
note_13: A double attack: the queen hits f7 and b7 at once. Black has to give something up.
note_18: The pawn opens lines towards a king that never castled. White will use it.
note_19: A knight sacrifice for the attack: Black's king is stuck in the centre and the lines towards it open.
note_25: The rook is given for the knight to open the d-file. The second rook is on its way.
note_31: The queen is given to lure the knight away from d7. Can you see mate in one?
note_33: Mate. Two weak opening moves — and the game is over on move 17.
feats_title: Opponent, coach and puzzles — in one place
feats_sub: Everything below is a working piece of the section, not a picture.
f_coach_t: A coach that explains in words
f_coach_d: After each move — a grade by colour and icon. Tap “Why?” for one or two sentences: what was missed and which move is stronger.
f_coach_say: The bishop on c4 is already eyeing f7. Close that diagonal before you bring the knight out.
f_engine_d: Eight bots, one per engine level, from first games to master. Five more are characters with a favourite opening.
f_path_t: 50,000 puzzles and a path of steps
f_path_d: Lichess puzzles picked for your rating. Every clean solve is a step on the map, and your piece grows from pawn to king.
f_online_t: Rated online play and a streak flame
f_online_d: Rated games against real opponents. Play or solve every day — the streak grows, and badges unlock rewards.
f_review_d: Every move gets a class, from “brilliant” to “blunder”. Plus accuracy for both sides, an evaluation graph and key moments.
f_skins_d: Classic, marble, Vikings, Monsters, Candy and Nightmares. Some sets unlock with badges.
f_tutor_t: A tutor and a board in the call
f_tutor_d: Find a chess tutor and go through games in class: a shared board right in the video call, both of you see every move.
a1: Yes. Bot games, puzzles, online play and game review are free. A VIP subscription only lifts the daily limit on coach explanations.
q2: How many explanations does the coach give?
a2: Move grades by colour and icon are unlimited — the engine computes them right in your browser. Explanations in words: 5 a day as a guest, 100 once signed in, unlimited with VIP.
a3: With the Elo system. An online game changes both players' ratings. Puzzles have their own rating: only the first attempt counts, and new puzzles are picked close to your level.
a4: Not to play bots or solve puzzles. An account is needed for online games, streaks, badges and saved progress.
q5: Can I study with a tutor?
a5: Yes. The catalogue has chess tutors, and the video call opens a shared board: the position and moves stay in sync for both of you.
q6: Which devices does it work on?
a6: Any modern browser — desktop, tablet and phone. Nothing to install: the engine runs right on the page.
final_title: Your first game is a minute away
final_sub: Pick an opponent, switch on the coach and watch your game change.
